questions.q: Water tankers fill three overhead tanks in a housing society. Tank P had 2,345 litres and received 478 litres. Tank Q had 2,341 litres and received 485 litres. Without adding the numbers in full, and explaining your reasoning each time: (a) compare 2,345 + 478 and 2,341 + 485 using <, > or =; (b) compare 912 − 268 and 915 − 271 (the water left in two other tanks after use); (c) compare 650 − 139 and 648 − 142. (d) Tank S had 2,346 litres. How many litres must it receive so that it ends with exactly as much water as Tank Q? Find it by reasoning from Tank Q's numbers.
questions.a: (a) P started 4 litres more than Q but received 7 litres fewer, so Q ends 3 litres more: 2,345 + 478 < 2,341 + 485 (2,823 and 2,826). (b) The second tank started with 3 litres more and also used 3 litres more, so the amounts left are equal: 912 − 268 = 915 − 271 (644 each). (c) The first starts 2 more and loses 3 fewer, so it ends 2 + 3 = 5 more: 650 − 139 > 648 − 142 (511 and 506). (d) S starts 2,346 − 2,341 = 5 litres more than Q, so it must receive 5 litres fewer than 485, that is 480 litres (2,346 + 480 = 2,826).
s: (a) Reasons that P is 4 ahead but gets 7 fewer, so writes 2,345 + 478 < 2,341 + 485
(b) Reasons that both the starting amount and the amount used are 3 more, so writes = (both 644)
(c) Reasons that the first is 2 more and loses 3 fewer, so 5 more, and writes >
(d) Finds that S starts 5 litres more than Q, so it must receive 485 − 5 = 480 litres

questions.q: A fruit seller at the weekly market in Nashik starts the day with 7 notes of ₹50, 4 notes of ₹10 and 12 coins of ₹2 in her cash box. She pays a porter 2 of the ₹50 notes and 5 of the ₹2 coins, and nothing else goes in or out. (a) Write one expression, using products, for the money left in the box, write it as a sum of terms with their signs, and find its value. (b) She then remembers that she actually paid the porter 3 of the ₹50 notes, not 2. Without working out the whole expression again, say which term changes, by how much, and find the new amount left. (c) Her son wrote 7 × 50 + 4 × 10 + 12 × 2 − 2 × 50 + 5 × 2 for part (a). Which term has the wrong sign, and by how many rupees is his value wrong? (d) She must keep at least ₹250 in the box. After the payment in (b), a customer asks for ₹30 in change. Can she give it? If not, find the most change she can give using only ₹2 coins, using the terms to justify.
questions.a: (a) 7 × 50 + 4 × 10 + 12 × 2 − 2 × 50 − 5 × 2 = 7 × 50 + 4 × 10 + 12 × 2 + (−2 × 50) + (−5 × 2); the terms are 7 × 50, 4 × 10, 12 × 2, −2 × 50 and −5 × 2, and the value is 350 + 40 + 24 − 100 − 10 = ₹304. (b) Only the term −2 × 50 changes; it becomes −3 × 50, which is 50 less, so the amount left is 50 less: 304 − 50 = ₹254. (c) The last term should be −5 × 2 (coins paid out), not +5 × 2. His value is 324, which is ₹20 too much: he added 10 instead of taking away 10, a difference of 2 × 10 = 20. (d) No: 254 − 30 = 224, which is less than 250. She can give away at most 254 − 250 = ₹4 without going below ₹250, that is 2 coins of ₹2 (she still has 12 − 5 = 7 such coins, so 2 is possible).
s: (a) Writes the expression with the two subtracted products, lists the five terms with their signs, and gets ₹304
(b) Names −2 × 50 as the only term that changes, says it becomes 50 less, and gets ₹254 without re-evaluating
(c) Names +5 × 2 as the wrong term and shows his value 324 is ₹20 too much (10 added instead of taken away)
(d) Shows 254 − 30 = 224 < 250, so No, and finds the most is ₹4, that is 2 coins of ₹2

questions.q: You are given that 284 + (−97) + 6 × 15 = 277. Without working out any expression in full, use how the terms have changed to answer. (a) Name the term that changes in 284 + (−95) + 6 × 15 and find its value. (b) Find the value of 284 + (−97) + 7 × 15. (c) Find the value of 288 + (−97) + 6 × 14, in which two terms have changed. (d) Raju says: 'If I make 284 four less and also make −97 four more, the value stays 277. In the same way, if I make 284 four less and change 6 × 15 to 7 × 15, the value also stays 277.' Is Raju right, partly right or wrong? Justify each half by comparing the terms.
questions.a: (a) Only the term −97 changes; −95 is 2 more than −97, so the value is 2 more: 279. (b) 7 × 15 is 15 more than 6 × 15, so the value is 15 more: 292. (c) 288 is 4 more than 284, and 6 × 14 is 6 less than 6 × 15, so the value changes by 4 − 6 = −2, that is 2 less: 275. (d) Partly right. The first half is right: 280 + (−93) + 6 × 15 has one term 4 less and another 4 more, so the changes cancel and the value is 277 (280 − 93 + 90 = 277). The second half is wrong: the first term is 4 less but the product is 15 more, so the value is 11 more: 280 + (−97) + 7 × 15 = 288, not 277.
s: (a) Names −97 as the changed term, reasons it is 2 more, and gives 279
(b) Reasons 7 × 15 is 15 more than 6 × 15 and gives 292
(c) Reasons the first term is 4 more and the product 6 less, so the value is 2 less: 275
(d) Says Raju is partly right: the first change cancels (277), but the second gives 11 more (288)

questions.q: Arvind adds the daily sales of his juice stall for 12 days and gets a total of ₹15,386. Then he notices two mistakes: he typed one day's sales of ₹2,749 as ₹2,479, and he forgot to take away a refund of ₹315 that he gave a customer. (a) Does he have to add all 12 numbers again? Explain using the properties of adding terms. (b) Write one expression, starting from 15,386, for the correct total. (c) Group the terms of your expression so that it is quick to work out, and say which property lets you group them that way. (d) Find the correct total and say by how much the first total was wrong.
questions.a: (a) No. The total is a sum of terms, and terms can be added in any order and grouped in any way (commutative and associative properties), so he can take out the wrong term and add the correct one and the refund at the end. (b) 15,386 − 2,479 + 2,749 − 315, that is 15,386 + (−2,479) + 2,749 + (−315). (c) Put the three correction terms side by side and add them first: −2,479 + 2,749 = 270, and 270 − 315 = −45, so the total is 15,386 + (−45); moving the correction terms next to each other uses the commutative property and adding them first as a group uses the associative property. (d) ₹15,341; the first total was ₹45 too much.
s: (a) Says he need not start again, because the order and grouping of terms do not change the sum
(b) Writes 15,386 − 2,479 + 2,749 − 315 (or the same as a sum of terms)
(c) Groups the correction terms, e.g. −2,479 + 2,749 = 270, then 270 − 315 = −45, naming the associative (or commutative) property
(d) Gives the correct total ₹15,341 and says the first total was ₹45 too much

questions.q: Consider the expression 60 − 36 ÷ 4 + 2 × 7. (a) Write it as a sum of terms and find its value. (b) Place one pair of brackets in it so that its value becomes 20. Show the working. (c) Place one pair of brackets so that its value becomes 18, and explain how the bracket changes what 36 is divided by. (d) Rehana says that, of all the ways of placing one pair of brackets in this expression, (60 − 36 ÷ 4 + 2) × 7 gives the greatest value. Find its value and explain, by comparing it with your answer to (a), why this placement makes the value so large.
questions.a: (a) 60 + (−36 ÷ 4) + 2 × 7 = 60 − 9 + 14 = 65. (b) (60 − 36) ÷ 4 + 2 × 7 = 24 ÷ 4 + 14 = 6 + 14 = 20. (c) 60 − 36 ÷ (4 + 2) × 7 = 60 − 6 × 7 = 60 − 42 = 18. Without the bracket 36 is divided by 4 only; with it, 36 is divided by 4 + 2 = 6, and the result 6 is then multiplied by 7, so the term taken away grows from 9 to 42. (d) Rehana is right: (60 − 36 ÷ 4 + 2) × 7 = (60 − 9 + 2) × 7 = 53 × 7 = 371. In (a) the 7 multiplies only the 2, adding 14; here it multiplies the whole sum 53, so the value is 7 times 53. The other placements give 20, 18, 37, 58, 65 or −17, all smaller.
s: (a) Identifies the terms 60, −36 ÷ 4 and 2 × 7 and gets 65
(b) Writes (60 − 36) ÷ 4 + 2 × 7 and shows 6 + 14 = 20
(c) Writes 60 − 36 ÷ (4 + 2) × 7, shows 60 − 42 = 18, and says 36 is now divided by 6, not 4
(d) Gets 53 × 7 = 371 and explains that the 7 now multiplies the whole sum instead of only the 2

questions.q: To subtract 198 from a number, Jaya subtracts 200 and then adds 2. To subtract 47 from 836, Kiran subtracts 50 and then subtracts 3 more, and gets 783. (a) Using a bracket, show why Jaya's method always works, and use it to find 1,563 − 198. (b) Write Kiran's steps as one expression with a bracket and say what number he has really taken away. (c) Find the correct value of 836 − 47 and explain why Kiran's answer is 6 less, not 3 less. (d) Make a quick strategy of your own for subtracting 302 using 300, explain it with a bracket, and use it to find 1,563 − 302.
questions.a: (a) 198 = 200 − 2, so for any number, say 1,563: 1,563 − 198 = 1,563 − (200 − 2) = 1,563 − 200 + 2, because removing a bracket after a minus sign changes the sign of every term inside. This gives 1,363 + 2 = 1,365, and the same steps work whatever the starting number is. (b) 836 − 50 − 3 = 836 − (50 + 3) = 836 − 53, so he has taken away 53, not 47. (c) 836 − 47 = 836 − (50 − 3) = 836 − 50 + 3 = 789. He should have added back 3 but took away 3 more, so he is off by 3 + 3 = 6 (789 − 783 = 6). (d) 302 = 300 + 2, so subtracting 302 is subtracting 300 and then 2 more: 1,563 − 302 = 1,563 − (300 + 2) = 1,563 − 300 − 2 = 1,263 − 2 = 1,261.
s: (a) The mark is for writing 1,563 − (200 − 2) = 1,563 − 200 + 2 with the reason for the sign change; the value 1,365 must follow
(b) Writes Kiran's steps as 836 − (50 + 3) and says he took away 53
(c) The mark is for explaining the error of 6 (3 taken away instead of 3 added), supported by the correct value 836 − 50 + 3 = 789
(d) Gives subtract 300 then subtract 2 more, justified by 1,563 − (300 + 2) = 1,563 − 300 − 2, and finds 1,261

questions.q: A school library has 460 books on its shelves when it opens. In the morning 85 books are issued and 23 are returned. In the afternoon 64 are issued and 38 are returned. The librarian writes the books on the shelves after the morning as 460 − (85 − 23); her assistant writes 460 − (85 + 23). (a) Explain what the bracket (85 − 23) stands for, find the librarian's value, and say by how many books the assistant's value is wrong and why. (b) For the end of the day the librarian writes 460 − (85 − 23) − (64 − 38). Remove both brackets, explaining the signs, and find the value. (c) The assistant now writes 460 − (85 + 64) + (23 + 38). Without working it out in full, say whether it gives the same number as part (b) and give your reason. (d) The librarian wants to write the whole day as 460 − (a single number). Find that number from the terms and say whether the shelves gained or lost books over the day.
questions.a: (a) 85 − 23 = 62 is the net number of books that left the shelves in the morning, so 460 − (85 − 23) = 460 − 62 = 398 books. The assistant's 460 − (85 + 23) = 460 − 85 − 23 = 352 also takes away the 23 books that came back, so it is 398 − 352 = 46 too few, that is the 23 counted wrongly twice (2 × 23 = 46). (b) 460 − (85 − 23) − (64 − 38) = 460 − 85 + 23 − 64 + 38 = 372 books; 23 and 38 change from minus to plus because each bracket is preceded by a minus sign. (c) Yes, it gives 372. Removing the bracket after the minus gives −85 − 64, and removing the bracket after the plus keeps +23 + 38, so the expression is 460 − 85 − 64 + 23 + 38: the same terms as in (b), only in a different order, and the order of terms does not change the value. (d) The number taken away is 85 + 64 − 23 − 38 = 88, so the day is 460 − 88 = 372. It is positive, so the shelves lost 88 books over the day.
s: (a) Explains (85 − 23) as the net books that left, gets 398, and shows the assistant is 46 too few (the 23 returned taken away instead of added)
(b) Removes both brackets with the signs changed, 460 − 85 + 23 − 64 + 38, and gets 372
(c) Says yes (372): after removing the brackets the terms are the same as in (b), only reordered
(d) Finds 85 + 64 − 23 − 38 = 88, writes 460 − 88 = 372, and says the shelves lost 88 books

questions.q: A school orders sports T-shirts at ₹165 each: 37 for Red House and 28 for Blue House. (a) Write two different expressions for the total cost, one as a sum of two products and one as a single product. (b) Find the total cost using the easier of the two. (c) The shop then gives ₹15 off on every T-shirt. Write the new total as one product with a bracket, use the distributive property to show how much the school saves, and find the new total. (d) The office clerk works out the new total as 65 × 165 − 15 = ₹10,710. Explain the clerk's mistake.
questions.a: (a) 37 × 165 + 28 × 165 and (37 + 28) × 165. (b) (37 + 28) × 165 = 65 × 165 = ₹10,725. (c) 65 × (165 − 15) = 65 × 165 − 65 × 15 = 10,725 − 975 = ₹9,750; the saving is 65 × 15 = ₹975. (d) The clerk took ₹15 off only once, as if one T-shirt was cheaper. The ₹15 comes off each of the 65 T-shirts, so 65 × 15 = 975 must be subtracted, not 15; his bill is ₹960 too high (10,710 − 9,750).
s: (c) Writes 65 × (165 − 15) = 65 × 165 − 65 × 15, gives the saving ₹975 and the new total ₹9,750
(d) Explains that 15 must be multiplied by 65 because the discount is on every T-shirt (bill ₹960 too high)

questions.q: A hostel in Anand needs at least 2,450 litres of milk over 4 weeks. Dairy A will supply 98 litres every day of the 4 weeks except on 3 days when the hostel is closed. Dairy B will supply 102 litres a day, but only on 24 days. (a) Write one expression for the milk Dairy A supplies in the 4 weeks. (b) Find its value quickly by writing 98 as a round number minus a small number. (c) Find Dairy B's total quickly in the same way, writing 102 as a round number plus a small number. (d) Which dairy should the hostel choose to meet its need? Justify using your answers.
questions.a: (a) (4 × 7 − 3) × 98 = 25 × 98 litres. (b) 25 × 98 = 25 × (100 − 2) = 2,500 − 50 = 2,450 litres. (c) 24 × 102 = 24 × (100 + 2) = 2,400 + 48 = 2,448 litres. (d) Dairy A: it supplies exactly 2,450 litres, which meets the need, while Dairy B supplies 2,448 litres, 2 litres short, even though it gives more milk each day.
s: (a) Writes (4 × 7 − 3) × 98, that is 25 × 98
(d) Chooses Dairy A because 2,450 meets the need and Dairy B is 2 litres short
